functions.name: shaderc_compiler_initialize
functions.description: Creates and returns a new compiler handle used to compile shaders. Returns NULL on initialization failure. Intended as the starting point before any compilation calls; can be created per use or retained and reused across threads with appropriate synchronization.
requirements: May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL before use.
Object is an opaque handle; only use with shaderc_* APIs that accept shaderc_compiler_t.

Thread-safety: concurrent calls on DIFFERENT compiler objects require no synchronization; concurrent calls on the SAME object require synchronization if and only if some calls take a non-const argument.
Must be released with shaderc_compiler_release when no longer needed.

functions.name: shaderc_compiler_release
functions.description: Releases resources held by a compiler handle. After return, the handle becomes invalid for any future calls.
requirements: compiler must be a shaderc_compiler_t returned by shaderc_compiler_initialize.
After this call, the compiler handle must not be used in any other function.
Caller must ensure no concurrent operations are using the same compiler at the time of release.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_initialize
functions.description: Creates a new, default-initialized set of compile options for customizing compilation. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: May return NULL on failure; caller must check for NULL before use.
Only use with shaderc APIs expecting shaderc_compile_options_t.
Must be released with shaderc_compile_options_release when no longer needed.
Thread-safety: basic guarantee (different objects require no sync; same object requires sync if any call takes a non-const argument).

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of an existing compile-options object. If NULL is passed, behaves like shaderc_compile_options_initialize.
requirements: If options is NULL, returns a new default-initialized options object (or NULL on failure).
Result must be released with shaderc_compile_options_release.
Thread-safety: basic guarantee as documented for options objects.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_release
functions.description: Releases resources held by a compile-options object. Safe to pass NULL; in that case, no action is taken.
requirements: If options is non-NULL, it must be a valid shaderc_compile_options_t previously created by initialize/clone.
After release, the options object must not be used in any further calls.
Safe to call with NULL.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_add_macro_definition
functions.signature: void shaderc_compile_options_add_macro_definition(shaderc_compile_options_t options, const char* name, size_t name_length, const char* value, size_t value_length);
functions.description: Adds or replaces a predefined macro definition to be used during compilation (equivalent to -Dname[=value]). Supports valueless macros when value is NULL or value_length is 0.
requirements: options must be a valid compile-options object.
name must point to a buffer of at least name_length bytes; the string data must remain valid for the duration of the call.
If adding a valueless macro, value must be NULL or value_length must be 0.
If a macro with the same name was previously added, its value is replaced by the new one.
value, if non-NULL and value_length > 0, must point to a buffer of at least value_length bytes; the data must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_source_language
functions.description: Sets the source language for compilation (GLSL by default).
requirements: options must be valid.
lang must be a valid shaderc_source_language enum value.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_generate_debug_info
functions.description: Enables generation of debug information in the compilation output.
requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_optimization_level
functions.description: Sets the desired optimization level for compilation. If set multiple times, the last call takes effect.
requirements: options must be valid.
level must be a valid shaderc_optimization_level value.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_forced_version_profile
functions.signature: void shaderc_compile_options_set_forced_version_profile(shaderc_compile_options_t options, int version, shaderc_profile profile);
functions.description: Forces GLSL version and profile, overriding any #version directive in the source. Use shaderc_profile_none for versions without profiles (e.g., <150).
requirements: options must be valid.
version must match GLSL #version numbering (integer, e.g., 450).
profile must be a valid shaderc_profile value; use shaderc_profile_none for versions without profiles.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_include_callbacks
functions.signature: void shaderc_compile_options_set_include_callbacks(shaderc_compile_options_t options, shaderc_include_resolve_fn resolver, shaderc_include_result_release_fn result_releaser, void* user_data);
functions.description: Registers client-provided callbacks to resolve and release #include requests during preprocessing/compilation. The includer owns the returned include_result and its contents until the release callback is invoked.
requirements: options must be valid.
resolver and result_releaser must be valid function pointers implementing the required contracts.
Include result lifetime: includer owns the result object and its contents; both must remain valid until result_releaser is called for that result.
To signal an include error from resolver, set include_result->source_name to an empty string and put the error message in include_result->content.
user_data is passed verbatim to the callbacks and may be NULL.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_suppress_warnings
functions.description: Suppresses emission of warnings. Overrides warnings-as-errors mode when both are set (warnings will be inhibited and not promoted to errors).
requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_target_env
functions.signature: void shaderc_compile_options_set_target_env(shaderc_compile_options_t options, shaderc_target_env target, uint32_t version);
functions.description: Sets the target shader environment (e.g., Vulkan or OpenGL) and its version, affecting diagnostics and semantics. Version 0 maps to Vulkan 1.0 for Vulkan target or OpenGL 4.5 for OpenGL target.
requirements: options must be valid.
target must be a valid shaderc_target_env value.
version must be either 0 or a value listed in shaderc_env_version per the included headers; 0 has the documented mapping.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_target_spirv
functions.description: Sets the target SPIR-V version to generate. Defaults depend on the target environment (e.g., SPIR-V 1.0 for Vulkan 1.0, 1.3 for Vulkan 1.1).
requirements: options must be valid.
version must be a valid shaderc_spirv_version value that the target environment can consume.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_warnings_as_errors
functions.description: Treats all warnings as errors. Note: suppress-warnings overrides this (warnings will not be emitted as errors when both are set).
requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_limit
functions.signature: void shaderc_compile_options_set_limit(shaderc_compile_options_t options, shaderc_limit limit, int value);
functions.description: Sets a specific resource limit used during compilation/validation (e.g., max lights, texture units, etc.).
requirements: options must be valid.
limit must be a valid shaderc_limit enum value.
value must be an integer appropriate for the specified limit (range constraints not specified in this header).

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_auto_bind_uniforms
functions.description: Enables or disables automatic assignment of descriptor bindings to uniforms that lack explicit bindings in the source.
requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_auto_combined_image_sampler
functions.description: Enables or disables automatic removal of separate sampler variables and conversion of image variables to combined image-samplers.
requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_hlsl_io_mapping
functions.description: Enables or disables use of HLSL IO mapping rules for bindings (defaults to false).
requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_hlsl_offsets
functions.description: When enabled, uses HLSL packing rules to determine block member offsets instead of standard GLSL rules. Only affects GLSL compilation; HLSL compilation always uses HLSL rules.
requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_binding_base
functions.signature: void shaderc_compile_options_set_binding_base(shaderc_compile_options_t options, shaderc_uniform_kind kind, uint32_t base);
functions.description: Sets the base binding number for a uniform resource kind when auto-assigning bindings. For GLSL, sets the lowest assigned number; for HLSL, the register number is added to this base.
requirements: options must be valid.
kind must be a valid shaderc_uniform_kind value.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_binding_base_for_stage
functions.signature: void shaderc_compile_options_set_binding_base_for_stage(shaderc_compile_options_t options, shaderc_shader_kind shader_kind, shaderc_uniform_kind kind, uint32_t base);
functions.description: Like set_binding_base but applies only to a specific shader stage (vertex, fragment, tess control/eval, geometry, or compute).
requirements: options must be valid.
shader_kind must be a valid specific stage kind; intended stages: vertex, fragment, tessellation evaluation, tessellation control, geometry, compute.
kind must be a valid shaderc_uniform_kind value.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_preserve_bindings
functions.description: Controls whether to preserve all declared bindings even if unused.
requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_max_id_bound

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_auto_map_locations

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_hlsl_register_set_and_binding_for_stage

functions.description: For the given shader stage, associates an HLSL register with a descriptor set and binding. The function keeps an internal copy of the string data.

shader_kind must be a valid shader stage kind.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_hlsl_functionality1

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_hlsl_16bit_types

requirements: options must be valid.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_options_set_nan_clamp

functions.name: shaderc_compile_into_spv
functions.signature: shaderc_compilation_result_t shaderc_compile_into_spv(const shaderc_compiler_t compiler, const char* source_text, size_t source_text_size, shaderc_shader_kind shader_kind, const char* input_file_name, const char* entry_point_name, const shaderc_compile_options_t additional_options);
functions.description: Compiles GLSL/HLSL source into a SPIR-V binary module. Shader kind can be forced, inferred from source via pragma, or defaulted. input_file_name is a null-terminated tag for diagnostics; entry_point_name is the null-terminated entry point. Returns a result object holding output and messages, or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: compiler must be a valid compiler handle; may be used concurrently per documented thread-safety (calls on the same object require synchronization if any call takes a non-const argument).
source_text must point to at least source_text_size bytes of source code.

shader_kind controls kind inference: if set to shaderc_glsl_infer_from_source, source must contain a supported #pragma annotation or compilation will error; if set to a default shader kind, that kind is used if inference fails.
input_file_name must be a null-terminated C string (used for diagnostics; need not be an actual file).
entry_point_name must be a null-terminated C string naming the entry point.
additional_options may be NULL or a valid compile-options object.
On success, caller must release the returned result with shaderc_result_release.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_into_spv_assembly
functions.signature: shaderc_compilation_result_t shaderc_compile_into_spv_assembly(const shaderc_compiler_t compiler, const char* source_text, size_t source_text_size, shaderc_shader_kind shader_kind, const char* input_file_name, const char* entry_point_name, const shaderc_compile_options_t additional_options);
functions.description: Compiles source like shaderc_compile_into_spv, but returns SPIR-V assembly text instead of a binary module. Assembly syntax matches SPIRV-Tools.
requirements: Same requirements as shaderc_compile_into_spv regarding parameters and thread-safety.
Result must be released with shaderc_result_release.

functions.name: shaderc_compile_into_preprocessed_text
functions.signature: shaderc_compilation_result_t shaderc_compile_into_preprocessed_text(const shaderc_compiler_t compiler, const char* source_text, size_t source_text_size, shaderc_shader_kind shader_kind, const char* input_file_name, const char* entry_point_name, const shaderc_compile_options_t additional_options);
functions.description: Runs preprocessing on the source and returns the preprocessed text instead of SPIR-V output.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid, interesting arbitrary strings to feed shaderc fuzzers
# expecting macro names/values, HLSL register/set/binding strings, and includer filenames/contents.
# It returns a bytes buffer which the fuzzing harness will use via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# We pack multiple candidate strings separated by NULs so the fuzzer can slice them or read them as needed.

_MAX_BYTES = 4096

_IDENTIFIER_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
_IDENTIFIER_BODY = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = rng.choice(_IDENTIFIER_START)
    s += "".join(rng.choice(_IDENTIFIER_BODY) for _ in range(max(0, n - 1)))
    return s


def _rand_number_str(rng: random.Random, signed: bool = False, max_digits: int = 5) -> str:
    if signed and rng.random() < 0.3:
        sign = rng.choice(["+", "-"])
    else:
        sign = ""
    # allow hex sometimes for registers like t0/u1 etc. but for numbers keep decimal
    digits = str(rng.randint(0, 10 ** max_digits - 1))
    return sign + digits


def _rand_macro_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a variety of macro values: empty, integer, float, string-literal-like, expression
    choice = rng.randint(0, 6)
    if choice == 0:
        return ""  # valueless
    if choice == 1:
        return _rand_number_str(rng, signed=True, max_digits=9)
    if choice == 2:
        # float-like
        return f"{rng.randrange(0, 1000)}.{rng.randrange(0, 100000):05d}"
    if choice == 3:
        # string literal style
        txt = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 12)
        return f'"{txt}"'
    if choice == 4:
        # identifier
        return _rand_ident(rng, 1, 24)
    if choice == 5:
        # expression
        a = _rand_number_str(rng, signed=True, max_digits=3)
        b = _rand_number_str(rng, signed=True, max_digits=3)
        op = rng.choice(["+", "-", "*", "/", "|", "&", "<<", ">>"])
        return f"({a}{op}{b})"
    # path-like
    parts = [_rand_ident(rng, 1, 6) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
    return "/".join(parts)


def _rand_hlsl_register_triplet(rng: random.Random):
    # HLSL registers like: t0, s1, u2, b3; sets/bindings as numeric strings or words
    reg_kind = rng.choice(["t", "s", "u", "b", "T", "S", "U", "B"])  # resource classes
    reg_idx = rng.randint(0, 63)
    reg = f"{reg_kind}{reg_idx}"

    # Descriptor set and binding often numeric; allow also named for variability
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        set_s = str(rng.randint(0, 31))
    else:
        set_s = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 8)

    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        binding_s = str(rng.randint(0, 255))
    else:
        binding_s = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 8)

    return reg, set_s, binding_s


def _rand_include_name_and_content(rng: random.Random):
    # Generate include path variations: relative, standard-like, nested, with extensions
    exts = [".glsl", ".h", ".inc", ".vert", ".frag"]
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_ident(rng, 1, 8))
    name = "/".join(parts) + rng.choice(exts)

    # Content: produce a tiny valid GLSL snippet or a simple macro line
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # macro header
        macro = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 16)
        val = _rand_macro_value(rng)
        if val == "":
            content = f"#ifndef {macro}\n#define {macro}\n#endif\n"
        else:
            content = f"#define {macro} {val}\n"
    else:
        # minimal GLSL snippet that can be included
        lines = []
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append("#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : enable")
        lines.append("// included file")
        # define a const or struct
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append(f"const int { _rand_ident(rng,1,8) } = {rng.randint(0,1024)};")
        else:
            lines.append(f"#define { _rand_ident(rng,1,8) } {rng.randint(0,256)}")
        content = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    return name, content


def _pool_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # 1) Macro names/values
    # Supply a mix of simple identifiers and complex patterns, ensure non-empty names.
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        name = _rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.choice([8, 16, 32]))
        out.append(name)
        # paired value options
        val = _rand_macro_value(rng)
        out.append(val)

    # Include names and contents
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        inc_name, inc_content = _rand_include_name_and_content(rng)
        out.append(inc_name)
        out.append(inc_content)

    # HLSL reg/set/binding triplets
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        reg, set_s, binding_s = _rand_hlsl_register_triplet(rng)
        out.append(reg)
        out.append(set_s)
        out.append(binding_s)

    # Additional useful tokens: numbers, expressions, quotes, spaces
    extra_tokens = [
        "0", "1", "2", "64", "128", "255", "1024", "-1", "+1",
        "(1+2)", "(8<<2)", "(a|b)", '"text"', "true", "false",
        # versions/profiles often parsed elsewhere but harmless as strings:
        "450", "460", "450core", "100es",
    ]
    out.extend(extra_tokens)

    # Ensure some longer content chunks but keep under size limits
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        big_comment = "//" + (" generated include content " * rng.randint(1, 10)).strip() + "\n"
        out.append(big_comment)

    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings = _pool_strings(rng)

    # Join as NUL-separated entries so the harness can consume multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    # from the same initial buffer. Ensure the total size cap.
    payload = b"\x00".join(s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore") for s in strings)

    # Guarantee at least one non-empty macro name at the start to satisfy stubs that require name_length>0
    if not strings or len(strings[0]) == 0:
        first = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 12).encode("utf-8")
        payload = first + b"\x00" + payload

    # Cap size
    if len(payload) > _MAX_BYTES:
        payload = payload[:_MAX_BYTES]
        # Avoid truncating in the middle of a UTF-8 sequence is acceptable since we ignore errors on decode,
        # and consumers treat as raw bytes/strings; still, ensure final byte isn't partial NUL structure
        # by appending a NUL terminator.
        if not payload.endswith(b"\x00"):
            payload += b"\x00"

    return payload

def random_weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[Tuple[str, float]]):
    total = sum(w for _, w in items)
    x = rng.random() * total
    for v, w in items:
        if x < w:
            return v
        x -= w
    return items[-1][0]

def make_glsl(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide whether to include a pragma to allow stage inference paths
    stage_key, pragma = rng.choice(GLSL_PRAGMA_STAGES)
    base = GLSL_SHADERS.get(stage_key, GLSL_SHADERS["vertex"])()

    # Randomly insert pragma at top to exercise shaderc_glsl_infer_from_source
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base = pragma + base

    # Sprinkle feature snippets
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        extra = "".join(rng.sample(GLSL_FEATURE_SNIPPETS, k=rng.randint(0, min(2, len(GLSL_FEATURE_SNIPPETS)))))
        base = extra + base

    # Optionally add a simple uniform/sampler to exercise bindings and mapping
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base += "uniform sampler2D s0;\n"
        if "fragment" in stage_key or rng.random() < 0.5:
            base += "layout(location=0) out vec4 out_color;\nvoid main(){ out_color = texture(s0, vec2(0.5)); }\n"

    return base

def make_hlsl(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    prof = random_weighted_choice(rng, [("ps", 0.5), ("vs", 0.35), ("cs", 0.15)])
    base = HLSL_SHADERS[prof]()

    # Add feature macros and an optional resource to exercise binding mapping
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        extra = "".join(rng.sample(HLSL_FEATURE_SNIPPETS, k=rng.randint(0, len(HLSL_FEATURE_SNIPPETS))))
        base = extra + base

    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = (
            "Texture2D t0 : register(t0);\nSamplerState s0 : register(s0);\n" + base
        )

    return base

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a content kind matching fuzzer sites that call FUZZ_PARAM_STR:
    # - GLSL/HLSL source (most common)
    # - Small identifiers for input filename or entry name
    # - Occasionally SPIR-V assembly to feed AssembleToSpv
    kind = random_weighted_choice(

    if kind == "glsl":

    s_bytes = s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    if len(s_bytes) > MAX_SIZE:

    return s_bytes

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for SPIR-V assembly text inputs. The fuzz stubs feed this into
# shaderc_assemble_into_spv / Compiler::AssembleToSpv. We must return bytes.
# Keep outputs valid (or at least well-formed enough) so the assembler explores
# code paths. Size capped under 4096 bytes.

_SPV_HEADER = [
    "; SPIR-V\n",
    "; Version: 1.0\n",
    "; Generator: 0\n",
    "; Bound: {bound}\n",
    "; Schema: 0\n",
]

# Minimal valid modules per stage, parameterized by entry point id and types.
# We vary capabilities and memory models to explore options.
def _minimal_vertex(bound_start: int, entry_name: str, memory_model: str) -> List[str]:
    # Simple vertex shader: empty function main that returns.
    # Uses GLSL450 memory model and Shader capability by default, configurable.
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"OpCapability Shader\n")
    lines.append(f"OpMemoryModel Logical {memory_model}\n")
    lines.append("OpEntryPoint Vertex %1 \"" + entry_name + "\"\n")
    lines.append("%2 = OpTypeVoid\n")
    lines.append("%3 = OpTypeFunction %2\n")
    lines.append("%1 = OpFunction %2 None %3\n")
    lines.append("%4 = OpLabel\n")
    lines.append("OpReturn\n")
    lines.append("OpFunctionEnd\n")
    return lines

def _minimal_fragment(entry_name: str, memory_model: str) -> List[str]:
    # Fragment shader writing a constant color to a location 0 output.
    lines = []
    lines.append("OpCapability Shader\n")
    lines.append(f"OpMemoryModel Logical {memory_model}\n")
    lines.append("OpEntryPoint Fragment %main \"" + entry_name + "\" %outColor\n")
    lines.append("OpExecutionMode %main OriginUpperLeft\n")
    lines.append("%void = OpTypeVoid\n")
    lines.append("%fn = OpTypeFunction %void\n")
    lines.append("%f32 = OpTypeFloat 32\n")
    lines.append("%v4f = OpTypeVector %f32 4\n")
    lines.append("%fp = OpTypePointer Output %v4f\n")
    lines.append("%outColor = OpVariable %fp Output\n")
    lines.append("%c0 = OpConstant %f32 0\n")
    lines.append("%c1 = OpConstant %f32 1\n")
    lines.append("%c = OpConstantComposite %v4f %c1 %c0 %c0 %c1\n")
    lines.append("%main = OpFunction %void None %fn\n")
    lines.append("%l = OpLabel\n")
    lines.append("OpStore %outColor %c\n")
    lines.append("OpReturn\n")
    lines.append("OpFunctionEnd\n")
    return lines

def _minimal_compute(entry_name: str, memory_model: str) -> List[str]:
    # Compute shader with a trivial main and a local size execution mode.
    lines = []
    lines.append("OpCapability Shader\n")
    lines.append(f"OpMemoryModel Logical {memory_model}\n")
    lines.append("OpEntryPoint GLCompute %main \"" + entry_name + "\"\n")
    lines.append("OpExecutionMode %main LocalSize 1 1 1\n")
    lines.append("%void = OpTypeVoid\n")
    lines.append("%fn = OpTypeFunction %void\n")
    lines.append("%main = OpFunction %void None %fn\n")
    lines.append("%l = OpLabel\n")
    lines.append("OpReturn\n")
    lines.append("OpFunctionEnd\n")
    return lines

_MEMORY_MODELS = ["GLSL450", "Vulkan", "OpenCL"]

# Optional decorations and capabilities to broaden coverage but keep validity.
_OPTIONAL_CAPS = [
    "Shader",
    "Int64",
    "Float64",
    "ImageQuery",
]

def _decorate_location_output() -> List[str]:
    # Add a separate output variable with location decoration to stress IO.
    lines = []
    lines.append("%i32 = OpTypeInt 32 1\n")
    lines.append("%vi2 = OpTypeVector %i32 2\n")
    lines.append("%poi = OpTypePointer Output %vi2\n")
    lines.append("%outPos = OpVariable %poi Output\n")
    lines.append("OpDecorate %outPos Location 0\n")
    return lines

def _header(bound: int) -> List[str]:
    return [s.format(bound=bound) for s in _SPV_HEADER]

def _compose_module(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose stage and memory model.
    stage = rng.choice(["vert", "frag", "comp"])  # vertex/fragment/compute
    memory_model = rng.choice(_MEMORY_MODELS)
    entry = rng.choice(["main", "Main", "entry", "csMain", "vsMain", "psMain"])

    # Sometimes add extra capabilities first.
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Choose a conservative bound; will be updated to a safe upper estimate.
    # Collect body then compute an upper bound id count heuristically.

    if stage == "vert":
        body = _minimal_vertex(1, entry, memory_model)
    elif stage == "frag":
        body = _minimal_fragment(entry, memory_model)
    else:
        body = _minimal_compute(entry, memory_model)

    # Optional decorations and extra caps.
    extras: List[str] = []
    if stage == "frag" and rng.random() < 0.6:
        extras.extend(_decorate_location_output())
    # Add 0-2 optional capabilities (avoid duplicates and keep Shader always included by bodies).
    opt_caps = rng.sample(_OPTIONAL_CAPS, k=rng.randint(0, 2))
    caps = []
    for c in opt_caps:
        if c != "Shader":
            caps.append(f"OpCapability {c}\n")

    # Compute a rough id bound: count % occurrences and add margin.
    temp_module = caps + body + extras
    id_count = sum(1 for l in temp_module for ch in l if ch == '%')
    bound = max(3, id_count + 3)

    # Assemble full module: header, capabilities, body, extras.
    mod: List[str] = []
    mod.extend(_header(bound))
    mod.extend(caps)
    mod.extend(body)
    mod.extend(extras)

    # Optionally append multiple entry points or execution modes to explore.
    if stage == "vert" and rng.random() < 0.3:
        mod.append("OpExecutionMode %1 OriginUpperLeft\n")
    if stage == "frag" and rng.random() < 0.3:
        mod.append("OpDecorate %outColor Location 0\n")

    text = "".join(mod)
    # Ensure final size constraint.
    if len(text) > 4000:
        text = text[:4000]
    return text

# Additionally provide a corpus of known-minimal valid assemblies including
# the exact one used by the C++ fuzzer for cross-coverage.
def _corpus() -> List[str]:
    asm_ok = (
        "; SPIR-V\n"
        "; Version: 1.0\n"
        "; Generator: 0\n"
        "; Bound: 3\n"
        "; Schema: 0\n"
        "OpCapability Shader\n"
        "OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450\n"
        "OpEntryPoint Vertex %1 \"main\"\n"
        "%2 = OpTypeVoid\n"
        "%1 = OpFunction %2 None\n"
        "OpLabel\n"
        "OpReturn\n"
        "OpFunctionEnd\n"
    )
    return [asm_ok]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # 50%: pick from curated corpus; 50%: generate stage-varied module.
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        txt = rng.choice(_corpus())
    else:
        txt = _compose_module(rng)
    # Return as bytes.
    return txt.encode("utf-8")
